ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, signatories and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU CFSP Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Consolidated List, and OFAC SDN List (banking-standard practice for Swift/TT rails); PEP and family-member/close-associate classification pursuant to FATF Recommendation 12 and Cyprus Law 188(I)/2007 as amended; adverse-media trawling in Greek, English, Russian and Chinese; re-screening every 90 days and on any event-triggered change; enhanced due diligence for PEPs and politically exposed persons; MOKAS suspicious transaction reporting thresholds and internal records retention of at least 5 years after business-relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRCOR) — Cyprus Business Registry electronic filing system (e-Companies/XBOnline platform; official URL: https://www.mcit.gov.cy/drcor)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted exclusively in Greek script and/or the Latin alphabet; names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Mandarin characters, Cyrillic) are inadmissible and must be romanized/transliterated into an approved English or Greek rendering. The legal suffix must be 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'ΛΙΜΙΤΕΔ' or 'ΛΤΔ'. The distinctive element will be refused if it conflicts with an existing registered name applying a visual and phonetic similarity test, or if it misleads as to the company's legal form or regulated activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A Cyprus name clearance is valid for 6 months and is not statutorily extendable; if the period lapses, the applicant must file a fresh name-reservation application and pay the applicable fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) submit a written reconsideration request to the Registrar within 14 days of the rejection, supplying consent letters from the competent licensing authority for any sensitive/prohibited token and addressing the similarity grounds; or (ii) lodge judicial review proceedings before the Administrative Court under Article 146 of the Constitution of Cyprus within 75 days of the refusal, seeking annulment on grounds of error of law, error of fact or disproportionality; urgent injunctive relief is available in exceptional cases.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered office. Every Cyprus private limited company must maintain a genuine physical registered office in Cyprus capable of receiving official correspondence and valid service of process under Companies Law Cap. 113, section 104. Virtual-office adjunct services may be utilized for administrative convenience but cannot replace the physical statutory address nor the Cyprus-resident company secretary.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk at 12-18% annual probability during the first trading year. Unannounced physical inspection exposure arises from the Cyprus Tax Department (VAT and Intrastat verification), Customs and Excise Department (EU import/export of dried botanical consignments), and the Social Insurance Services. Although the banking AML risk tier is 'Low_Risk_Standard', maintenance of board minutes, logistics contracts, pre-shipment inspection records and registered-office files at the physical address materially mitigates inspection disqualification risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Companies Law, Cap. 113 of Cyprus, as amended - Sections 3 (mode of forming company), 9 (memorandum), 10 (articles), 11 (declaration of compliance), 13 (certificate of incorporation), 30 (company seal), 33 (registered office) and 164-170 (directors and secretary).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRC), Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry, Nicosia, Cyprus
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application comprising the Memorandum of Association, Articles of Association, Declaration of Compliance (Form HE1), consents of directors and secretary (Forms HE2/HE3) and Notice of Registered Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private limited company under Cap. 113. Authorised capital is fixed in the Memorandum (commonly EUR 1,000 divided into 1,000 shares of EUR 1.00); shares may be issued partly paid unless the Articles provide otherwise. No escrow account, capital deposit or bank certificate is required at incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the incorporation of the Company be ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the allotment and issue of shares to the subscriber and initial members, as recorded in the register of members, be approved. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the Company be fixed at [registered address in the Republic of Cyprus]. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the directors and the company secretary named on incorporation be confirmed in office. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the directors be authorised to open and operate bank accounts, execute contracts, and make all registrations required by the Tax Department, Social Insurance Services and the Registrar. RESOLVED THAT the foregoing resolutions be entered in the minutes and copies placed in the Company's statutory registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRC) via the Cyprus Business Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed name for the private limited company through the Cyprus Business Portal or at the DRC counter. The name must include 'Limited' or 'Ltd', be distinctive, and not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or to a mark protected by the Trade Marks Law Cap. 268. Await the name approval notice before proceeding to filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed business object statement (ISIC 4631 / wholesale food distribution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried because of similarity, submit an administrative objection within 14 days or amend and resubmit the reserved name; urgent priority processing is available for an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed advocate/legal counsel in the Republic of Cyprus acting as the incorporator's agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in accordance with Cap. 113. Include an objects clause covering wholesale trade and international export of dried goji berries, herbal botanicals and related products, an authorised share capital clause, and a limited liability clause. Each subscriber must sign the memorandum before a witness; foreign subscribers must provide notarised passport copies.
required_dossiers: Form HE2 - Consent to act as director
Form HE3 - Consent to act as secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Counsel will correct defective articles or object clauses prior to filing; if the Registrar questions foreign execution, add apostille certification and re-execute within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation application with the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the full incorporation package electronically via the Cyprus Business Portal or at the DRC Nicosia counter. Pay the statutory incorporation fee (EUR 100) and registry stamp duties. The Registrar examines compliance with Sections 9-16 of Cap. 113 and issues the Certificate of Incorporation under Section 13.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, rectify the specified deficiency within 30 days; failure causes lapse. Refusal may be appealed under Section 14 of Cap. 113 within 14 days by lodging a sworn application with the District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and opening of statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver (DRC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and incorporation date. Obtain certified copies of the Memorandum and Articles, order the company seal if required by the Articles, and procure statutory books: register of members, register of directors and secretary, register of charges, and minute book.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply at the DRC counter for administrative rectification of clerical errors in the certificate (name, number or date) within 5 business days; the original certificate must be returned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation registrations with tax, social insurance and labour authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cyprus Tax Department; Social Insurance Services (SIS); District Labour Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company with the Cyprus Tax Department to obtain a Tax Identification Number (TIN). Apply for VAT registration under the VAT Law 94(I)/2000 when taxable turnover exceeds EUR 15,600 or for intra-Community acquisitions; voluntary VAT registration is advisable for export traders. Register as an employer with Social Insurance Services and notify the District Labour Office of commencement of business operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late registration penalties may be mitigated by voluntary self-disclosure; file written representations to the Commissioner of Taxation within 30 days of a penalty notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting and commencement of corporate governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or adopt a written resolution to: ratify the incorporation, approve the allotment of subscription shares, fix the registered office, confirm director and secretary appointments, authorise opening of bank accounts, and approve the common seal. Record minutes in the statutory minute book.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolutions (share allotment, registered office, officer appointments)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural defects in the first meeting may be cured by a subsequent written resolution of the directors ratifying all acts performed before the meeting.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Medical and Public Health Services, Ministry of Health of Cyprus (local District Health Offices) for food business registration; Department of Agriculture of the Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment for phytosanitary certification of exported dried goji berries and herbal botanicals
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Operator (FBO) Registration Certificate and Establishment Approval under the Control of Foodstuffs Law 54(I)/1996 and EU Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, together with an Exporter Phytosanitary Certificate for plant-origin consignments

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environment, Ministry of Agriculture, Rural Development and Environment, Cyprus
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B2 (screening tier): bulk storage and dry repacking of dried goji berries and herbal botanicals is normally exempt from a full EIA Report; the Department issues an Environmental Screening Exemption/Registration decision unless annual throughput or site capacity thresholds exceed Annex II criteria of Law 127(I)/2018.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Trade effluent and wastewater must comply with the Water Pollution Control Law 106(I)/2002 and EU Directive 91/271/EEC for discharge to municipal sewer; no significant VOC emissions from dry goods handling (de-minimis cleaning agent use); packaging waste recovery obligations under the Packaging Waste Law 32(I)/2002; waste handling and disposal in accordance with the Waste Management Law 185(I)/2011.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Fire Service of Cyprus under the Fire Prevention Law 21(I)/1992 (fire detection, extinguishers, emergency exits); structural load inspection certificate for warehouse racking and mezzanines; occupational health and safety (OHS) registration and risk assessment approval by the Department of Labour Inspection under Law 89(I)/1996 and the Safety and Health at Work Law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Department of Taxation, Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Cyprus (Tax Department); operating portal is the Cyprus Tax Portal, https://taxportal.mof.gov.cy (My Cyprus Tax / Taxisnet e-submissions). The VAT Service is integrated within the Tax Department. Exports are administered by the Cyprus Customs and Excise Department, Ministry of Finance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate a Private Limited Company (Ltd, HE77) with the Registrar of Companies (ROC, https://www.companies.gov.cy) and obtain Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, plus a registered office address in Cyprus. 2) Upon incorporation the Tax Department automatically issues the statutory 8-digit Tax Identification Code (TIC / TIN), which serves as the corporate tax number. 3) For VAT, file Form TFC 101 (Application for VAT Registration) electronically through the Tax Portal attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, director passports, registered office lease, and a business plan with projected turnover. 4) A non-resident company establishing a branch must first register the branch under Part XI of the Companies Law and obtain a branch TIC before any VAT or income tax registration. 5) Non-established foreign suppliers have a zero registration threshold and must register for VAT before the first taxable supply in Cyprus; a fiscal representative is required where the applicant is not established in an EU Member State and no administrative cooperation agreement exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Cyprus-resident Ltd is a company-level taxpayer on worldwide income at 12.5% under Income Tax Law 118(I)/2002; foreign permanent establishment profits are exempt under s.6 subject to conditions; dividends and capital gains from foreign participations benefit from the participation exemption; non-resident companies are taxed on Cyprus-source income only, giving the system a territorial-scope overlay; no pass-through or transparent classification exists for an Ltd).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Cyprus does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Statutory elections available to a Cypriot Ltd include: the Notional Interest Deduction (NID) election on new equity capital under s.9B (with 5-year carry-forward of unutilized amounts); group loss relief election under s.19 (donor surrenders up to 75% of taxable profit); the IP Box nexus election (80% of qualifying IP profit may benefit); election to exempt foreign permanent establishment profits under s.6(1)(c); unilateral Foreign Tax Credit election under s.32 rather than exemption; and VAT partial exemption annual adjustment election. Cyprus has enacted ATAD-aligned hybrid mismatch rules that constrain dual-inclusion and double-dip structures, so no hybrid mismatch election is available for imported mismatch outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / FPA) under the Value Added Tax Law 95(I)/2000, as amended, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 15,600 of taxable turnover in the preceding 12 months for Cyprus-established businesses (2025). Non-established taxable persons have a nil threshold and must register before the first taxable supply. The threshold for intra-EU distance sales to final consumers is EUR 35,000; the annual threshold for cross-border B2C telecommunications, broadcasting and e-services under the OSS scheme is EUR 10,000. Voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time B2B fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control or digital stamping regime is in force in Cyprus. Mandatory electronic filing applies: VAT return (Form TFC 211), VIES lists and Intrastat declarations must be submitted via the Cyprus Tax Portal by the 10th day of the second month following the tax period. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory under EU Directive 2014/55/EU using the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 standard. Export declarations are lodged electronically with Customs through the EU Export Control System (ECS) using the Single Administrative Document (SAD) EX/A, producing the Movement Reference Number (MRN). VAT invoices must satisfy Articles 122-126 of the VAT Law (sequential numbering, date, supplier and customer identification, description, quantities, net and VAT data); records must be retained for 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated treatment is available for a supply of goods dispatched or transported by the supplier, or by another person acting on the supplier's behalf, to a destination outside the EU, per s.15(v) of the VAT Law 95(I)/2000 (Art. 146(1)(a) of Directive 2006/112/EC). For dried goji berries and herbal botanicals the exporter must prove that the goods physically left the EU customs territory within 90 days of the time of supply (extensions possible where justified); the supplier must obtain and retain the customs export declaration and contemporaneous transport evidence within 3 months of supply; the commercial documentation must evidence the offshore recipient, payment terms and transfer of ownership; export-related services (freight, insurance, handling performed in Cyprus) may also be zero-rated where directly connected to and contractually embedded in the export supply; goods merely kept for exhibition or intended to be brought back into the EU do not qualify.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Single Administrative Document (SAD) EX/A with Movement Reference Number (MRN) lodged in the EU Export Control System (ECS)
Commercial invoice in the 10 mandatory VAT fields, sequentially numbered, referencing the export contract
Bill of Lading (ocean) / Airway Bill (air) / CMR or rail consignment note (land) proving physical dispatch from Cyprus to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / bank credit advise evidencing offshore payment and FX conversion
Phytosanitary certificate (EU plant health certificate under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/2072) for dried Lycium barbarum (goji) and herbal botanicals
Certificate of Origin (recommended for buyer customs clearance and documentary credit banks)
Proof of export identity (exporter EORI number and customs party role)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Tax Department and Customs conduct post-clearance audits and cross-check the MRN, movement records and payment flows. If the 90-day export deadline or the proof-of-export bundle is missing, the zero-rating is retrospectively overturned and the exporter is assessed to VAT at 19% plus statutory late interest at 1.5% per month and default-assessment penalties. Fraudulent export zero-rating or false customs declarations constitute criminal offenses under s.39 of the VAT Law 95(I)/2000, punishable by a fine of up to EUR 50,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 5 years, and under the Customs and Excise Law 94(I)/2004 false declarations expose the exporter to penalty assessments of up to three times the customs debt, forfeiture or sale of the goods, loss of EORI status and personal liability of directors; repayment claims and input VAT credits are clawed back where the underlying export is invalidated.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Cyprus (Κεντρική Τράπεζα της Κύπρου)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Cyprus is a Eurozone member state; the euro is fully convertible and there are no residual exchange controls. Both current account and capital account transactions are liberalised under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the free movement of capital regime. Non-resident dividends, profit remittances, loan repayments, and liquidation proceeds may be freely transferred once standard corporate tax withholding and anti-money laundering verification are satisfied. The only substantive friction is the mandatory EU sanctions and beneficial ownership screening applied by Cypriot banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or fixed repatriation timelines for export receipts in Cyprus. Exporters may hold foreign currency proceeds in designated accounts without conversion into euros. For external statistics and balance of payments data, the Central Bank of Cyprus requires banks to report the purpose and counterparty of export inflows, but no permission or approval is needed for the receipt or disposal of the funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Cyprus Public Company Ltd

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border digital EMI accounts are legally viable in Cyprus only where the provider is an authorised Electronic Money Institution under E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC, transposed nationally through the Electronic Money Law 122(I)/2012. EEA-licensed digital EMIs that passport into Cyprus are rated Medium viable, as they may open segregated e-money accounts and issue GBP, USD, or EUR IBANs with pass-through settlement. Offshore, non-EEA digital banks and unlicensed EMIs are Low viability and cannot lawfully carry on payment services or establish bank accounts in Cyprus. Any offshore EMI arrangement would require a Cypriot commercial bank intermediary and would trigger enhanced correspondent due diligence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The standard mandate for Cyprus corporate accounts requires at least one director or individually authorised signatory to attend a physical due diligence interview at the bank's compliance office. For low-risk international wholesale traders, selected banks permit remote onboarding using a valid passport, apostilled corporate documents, video identification, and certified copies, with the bank reserving the right to summon the beneficial owner for an in-person interview at any time. A fully remote account opening for non-resident companies is not universal and should be secured in advance through a relationship manager under the bank's delegated authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident one-hundred-percent owned Cyprus LTD with no previous banking footprint and a purely cross-border herbal trading model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, Register of Members and Directors, Certificate of Good Standing, Register of Beneficial Owners filed with the Cyprus Registrar of Companies, certified passports, proof of residential address, two independent bank references, wealth and source-of-funds declaration, unaudited or audited financial statements, and a detailed corporate structuring diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent disbursements to suppliers in emerging or high-risk jurisdictions against which the bank applies stricter sanctions and payment clearance rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file comprising signed purchase and sale agreements, pro forma invoices, commercial invoices, bills of lading, airway bills, CMR transport documents, Single Administrative Declaration (SAD), import/export customs entries, phytosanitary certificates, laboratory certificates of analysis for pesticide residuals and heavy metals, warehouse storage receipts, and final client purchase orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Share capital injections above EUR 100,000 without clear economic substance or traceable personal savings history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified bank statements evidencing the ultimate source of funds, signed statutory share subscription declarations, board minutes approving the capital increase, source-of-wealth report, audited financial statements showing fund utilisation, Cyprus Form FAR (Financial Activity Report) where applicable, and a notarised affidavit from the contributing shareholder explaining the accumulation of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner appears on PEP, sanction, adverse media, or politically exposed risk screening lists.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence report, independent World-Check or LexisNexis sanctions screening results, sworn explanation of the exposure, evidence of legitimate participation in the business, independent legal opinion from an international sanctions counsel, certified trust or corporate structure evidence, and an enforceable commitment to continuous transaction monitoring and quarterly compliance reviews.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is remitted through standard SWIFT MT103 messages from the overseas corporate bank to the Cyprus beneficiary account. The payment narrative in field 70 must explicitly state 'Share Capital Contribution' and reference the company's Memorandum and Articles of Association; the bank will request a board resolution and share allotment certificate as verification. For EUR transfers from EU/EEA members, SEPA-eligible wires are used. No Central Bank approval is required for third-country capital inflows; the applying bank classifies the funds as direct investment equity for balance of payments reporting and confirms the economic purpose before the account is credited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlement is executed predominantly via SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers for supplier invoices. Confirmed irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600 are used for high-value bulk GOJI consignments where documentary risk must be mitigated. For euro-denominated payments to European counterparties, SEPA Credit Transfer is accepted. Settlement integrity is preserved by the bank's requirement of all transport, customs, quality, and invoicing documents against the payment instruction, and every transfer is screened against sanctions lists before release.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form HE32) - company particulars and register of members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Registrar of Companies and Official Receiver, Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry (Nicosia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the annual general meeting; standard practice is filing on the anniversary of incorporation (commonly by the registration anniversary date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a default fine of EUR 50; persistent default leads to administrative strike-off from the Cyprus Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Company Levy (franchise fee for continued registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies (paid through the Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 June each calendar year (anniversary of calendar year, irrespective of incorporation date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs an automatic surcharge of EUR 50; if unpaid for more than 10 months beyond the due date, the Registrar may strike the company off the register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Annual Confirmation and Register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies (UBO Register maintained at Central Register of Beneficial Ownership)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days of the anniversary of incorporation; any UBO change must be filed within 14 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance triggers civil fines up to EUR 500 per breach; prolonged failure can result in strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form IR3) - annual tax declaration for the company's profits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months from the end of the calendar tax year (e.g., for tax year ending 31 December, return must be filed by 31 December of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Immediate EUR 100 penalty for late filing; additional EUR 50 per month (maximum 12 months); plus potential 5% surcharge on tax due for late payment

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies unless the company qualifies as a 'small company' under Cyprus Companies Law (Cap. 113) meeting at least two of three thresholds: balance sheet total not exceeding EUR 4,000,000, net turnover not exceeding EUR 8,000,000, average employees not exceeding 50; audit exemption is not available to public-interest entities, banks, insurance companies, or certain regulated activities
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the European Union; small companies may opt to apply the IFRS for SMEs framework or Cyprus Company Law accounting framework

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain an up-to-date statutory register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (PSC Register) at its registered office and file an annual confirmation with the Registrar of Companies within 60 days of each anniversary of incorporation; any change in UBO particulars must be filed within 14 days

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 600 per annum (typical registered office and company secretary service market range)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 - USD 2,500 per annum (typical certified audit fee for a small/medium-size trading company)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on new equity at the rate published yearly by the Cyprus Central Bank; IP Box regime for qualifying intangible property allowing an 80% deduction on qualifying profits (effective rate 2.5%); 50% deduction of expenditure for business premises used by disabled employees; group relief rules allow transfer of losses between group companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form T.D. 4 (Company Tax Return), e-filed through the Cyprus TaxisNet integrated tax portal at https://taxisnet.mof.gov.cy; paper submission requires express approval by the Tax Commissioner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the tax year is the calendar year unless a different accounting year is approved by the Cyprus Tax Department.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 12 months after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year company, the deadline is 31 December of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, company registration number (e.g., HE 77), and registered address as per the Cyprus Registrar of Companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident company with a Cyprus permanent establishment (PE), enter the Cypriot branch or PE registration identifiers and indicate the PE's legal address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Tax Year and Accounting Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the fiscal year end. If a non-calendar year has been approved, specify the period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the PE accounting period; the PE may have a closing date different from the head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Total Gross Income and Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate worldwide gross income, including export sales of organic dried lycium and herbal botanicals, adjusted for returns, allowances, and discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only profits attributable to the Cyprus PE, limited to Cyprus-source trading income and assets used by the PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs: purchased goods, freight and marine insurance, customs fees, packaging, warehousing, marketing, administrative salaries, rent, and maintenance of local facilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses must be incurred wholly and exclusively for the PE's trade, and head-office allocations must be supported by evidenced cost apportionment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Adjusted Taxable Profit or Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss multiplied by 12.5% CIT, adjusted for non-deductible expenditure, depreciation, provisions, capital gains, and allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE's accounting result is adjusted under Cyprus tax law; interest, royalties, and management charges that constitute Cyprus-source income are brought within this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on qualifying new equity, IP Box deduction, and other statutory incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Availability is limited; the PE may claim deductions solely to the extent allowed for Cyprus-resident trading entities, and subject to economic substance verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Tax Computation and Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 12.5% head-rate, deduct any foreign tax credit or relief, and calculate the final tax due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIT is charged on the PE's Cyprus taxable profit; unilateral and treaty foreign tax credits are available only for income genuinely taxed in the other State.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed by a director or the company secretary, confirming the accuracy of the return, identifying beneficial owners, and disclosing intercompany cross-border transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned Cyprus entity, include the ultimate beneficial owner's jurisdiction and tax identification number; disclose any controlled transactions requiring transfer-pricing documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: EUR 100 fixed, plus EUR 50 per month or part-month of continued default (maximum additional EUR 500). If tax remains unpaid by the statutory date, interest accrues at 3.5% per annum and a late-payment penalty of 5% on the unpaid amount is imposed. Extended non-compliance may instigate criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% – Cyprus does not impose withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, regardless of corporate shareholder status, provided the recipient does not maintain a permanent establishment in Cyprus. Cyprus-resident individual shareholders may be subject to Special Defence Contribution at 17% on dividend income, but non-residents are exempt.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Since no domestic WHT is withheld, the principal administrative requirement is evidentiary. A non-resident shareholder must supply a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence, confirm beneficial ownership, and if invoking the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, hold at least 5% of the paid-up share capital (or the lower threshold allowed by the applicable DTA), and complete a Cyprus Tax Department clearance form if claiming an early refund. The Cyprus company must retain the TRC and directive-specific declarations in its records.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory rate on interest and royalty payments made to non-resident payees not acting through a Cyprus PE; no Cyprus withholding tax is levied on outbound interest or royalties. Cyprus DTAs generally reduce treaty rates for residents of the other contracting state, commonly 0% to 5% on interest and 0% to 5% on royalties; a TRC is needed to invoke treaty protection, though no withholding occurs at source.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000 aggregate controlled transactions per tax year triggers mandatory preparation and retention of Local File documentation. A Master File is required when the Cyprus entity belongs to a multinational group whose consolidated revenue exceeds EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cyprus does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code, but applies economic-substance requirements through the tax-residency test (management and control in Cyprus), the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive (ATAD), and the Cyprus IP Box regime. Sufficiency of premises, employees, revenues, and business direction is assessed by the Cyprus Tax Department; artificial arrangements without genuine substance are disregarded for taxation and treaty eligibility.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully or negligently omitting export revenue, falsifying invoices, inflating purchases, concealing foreign bank accounts, or creating artificial losses to eliminate or reduce the 12.5% CIT liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at full 12.5% with 100% penalty on the under-assessed tax, default interest at 3.5% per annum, and criminal prosecution under the Cyprus Assessment and Collection of Taxes Law carrying a fine up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment up to three years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or participate in concealment are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, exposed to civil recovery proceedings, travel bans, and criminal imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced when fraud is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Cyprus private limited company without real commercial substance, without a physical office, without at least one independent director managing affairs in Cyprus, and using the entity solely as a round-tripping conduit for goji berry and herbal product proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Statutory strike-off or reversal of the Cypriot corporate identity, denial of treaty benefits on dividends/interest/royalties, retroactive taxation of profits at the ultimate parent shareholder level, and substantial administrative penalties for failure to maintain proper corporate records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the shell entity are personally assessed for the underlying tax liabilities if the company is shell-struck, and the Cyprus Court may issue a declaration of fraud or misfeasance, leading to disqualification from directorship, asset seizure within Cyprus, and restraint orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany purchase prices for dried botanicals, warehousing fees, or management charges outside the arm's length range, or failing to prepare a Local File where aggregate controlled transactions exceed EUR 750,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income to the arm's length price, additional Corporate Income Tax at 12.5%, penalty of 5% per month on the additional tax due, and fixed fines ranging from EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 for missing documentation; continued non-documentation attracts criminal fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve intentionally distorted pricing may be cited for aiding tax evasion, jointly liable for the adjusted tax, and subject to monetary penalties in cases of gross negligence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using proceeds from undeclared herbal-product exports to purchase Cypriot real estate, moving value through opaque Swift/TT arrangements without identifying beneficial owners, or executing payments to third-party shell accounts without verifying the corresponding trade.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Cyprus Prevention and Suppression of Money Laundering Activities Law, financial and non-financial entities face fines up to EUR 500,000, temporary suspension of the license to operate, confiscation of transaction proceeds, and criminal penalties against natural persons including imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial-owner nominees face personal criminal indictment; individual fines can be up to EUR 50,000, with imprisonment for conduct committed with intent; the regulatory authority may also issue travel bans pending criminal investigation and void corporate transactions.
